data: Is the total meeting time always longer than the time decisions are made?

The question asks whether the total meeting time is always longer than the time decisions are made. From the caption, we can see two lines representing the total meeting time and the time decisions are made. The red line represents the total meeting time, and the blue line represents the time decisions are made. 

By analyzing the graph, we can observe that the red line (total meeting time) is consistently above the blue line (time decisions are made) throughout the entire range of meetings. This indicates that the total meeting time is always longer than the time decisions are made. Therefore, the answer to the question is yes, the total meeting time is always longer than the time decisions are made.
